_doc: FIRST-PERSON defaults for the per-keeper logbook voice. Every writing STYLE in data/voices/*.json inherits this (merge order: data/chronicle-voice.json structural base <- THIS <- the style file), so a style need only override the flavour it wants and still renders cleanly. This is what turns a Story tab into a first-person log handed from keeper to keeper: `pronoun.<kind>.first` makes clauses that open on the entity's own name read as 'we/I', and `handover.<kind>.<cause>` is the note each new keeper writes on taking up the book. Restrained ship's-chronicle tone here; styles supply personality. TOKENS: {name} keeper's name · {rank} rank label (may be empty) · {rankc} '', or ', <rank>' (SAFE optional-rank — prefer this over {rank}) · {type} ship/island type · {ship} vessel name · {home} home port · {place} island name · {population} souls · {bounty} bounty · {ord} ordinal word · {foeName}/{foeHome} a recurring foe. Unknown/empty tokens collapse with adjacent glue.

founder: Here begins my keeping of this log. I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} answers to me now.
The book is mine to keep from today. I am {name}{rankc}, master of this {home} {type}, and I mean to fill her pages honestly.
A new hand opens this log — mine. I am {name}{rankc}; this {home} {type} and her account are both in my charge.
I take up the keeping of this book. I am {name}{rankc}, and every voyage of this {home} {type} will be set down here under my hand.
So begins my command, and my keeping of her log. I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} sails under me now.
The pen and the wheel both come to me this day. I am {name}{rankc}, and I'll keep this {home} {type}'s book as faithfully as I keep her course.
successor: The log passes into my hand. I am {name}{rankc}; her account goes on under me.
Her book comes to me now. I am {name}{rankc}, and I take up the tale where the last hand left it.
Command has changed, and the log with it. I am {name}{rankc}; I keep her chronicle from here.
I take up this book after another. I am {name}{rankc}, and her story goes on under my keeping.
The keeping of this log falls to me. I am {name}{rankc}; what came before I leave as it stands, and set down what comes next.
A fresh hand on the pen — mine. I am {name}{rankc}, and I mean to serve her as well as those before me.
mutiny: The crew put the old master over the side and pressed the book on me. I am {name}, green to command, and set down what I can.
They cast the captain out and made me keep this log in his place. I am {name}, new to the wheel, and doing my best by her.
The old master is gone, thrown over by his own crew, and the book is mine now. I am {name}, untried, and learning fast.
Mutiny put me here, pen in hand and hardly ready for it. I am {name}, and I'll keep her log as steady as I am able.
The men would not have the old captain, and it fell to me to take up his book. I am {name}, green enough, but hers to keep.
The crew rose, the master fell, and the log came to me. I am {name}, new-made and none too sure — but I'll write her true.
rogue: So ends my honest trade. I have run the black flag up with my own hands, and this crew has followed me to it — no more lawful cargoes, only what the sword will take.
I have done with fair dealing. The black flag flies from my own masthead now, by my own choosing, and this crew stands with me.
Let the ledgers rot. I raised the black flag myself, and my crew cheered it up the mast — we take what we please from here.
No more honest freight for me. I turned this ship to the black flag with my own hand, and there is no turning her back.
I chose the black flag, and I'll not pretend otherwise. My crew chose it with me, and this log goes on as a rover's from today.
The honest trade never paid what I was owed, so I took the black flag for myself. This crew is mine, this ship is mine, and what we take is ours.
pirate: The old master is gone — put ashore, or over the side. I am {name}{rankc}, and this hull answers to my black flag now; her honest days are done.
This ship has a new master, and it is me. I am {name}{rankc}; her old captain kept honest books — I keep a different kind entirely.
Her lawful master would not see reason, so we saw him off. I am {name}{rankc}, and the flag above her is black from this day.
A new hand takes up this book — mine. I am {name}{rankc}, and I did not come by this ship through honest trade.
The trader who kept this log is finished with her. I am {name}{rankc}, her master now, and there'll be no more talk of manifests and fair dealing.
She changed hands at the point of a cutlass, and the hand is mine. I am {name}{rankc}; the black flag suits her better than her old colours ever did.
They gave me the ship and the book both, whether they meant to or no. I am {name}{rankc}, and this hull sails under my black flag now.
I took command the only way worth taking it. I am {name}{rankc} — her past owner has no further say in where she sails, nor under what flag.
prize: She struck to us. I am {name}{rankc}; this hull sails under my flag now, and her log continues at the point of a cutlass.
We took her fair, in a hard fight. I am {name}{rankc}, her master now, and her book is mine to keep.
Her colours came down and ours went up. I am {name}{rankc}; this prize is mine, and I take up her log where her old captain dropped it.
She yielded, and I claimed her. I am {name}{rankc}, and this hull answers to my black flag from the moment she struck.
A prize, and a fine one. I am {name}{rankc}; I put a crew aboard and the book in my own pocket, and on she sails under me.
We boarded her and she was ours. I am {name}{rankc}, and her honest days ended the hour I stepped onto her deck.
recovered: A hunter ran us down and the black flag came down with him. I am {name}{rankc}, set to bring this hull back to honest trade — and to keep her book.
The rovers who held her are beaten, and she is a lawful ship again. I am {name}{rankc}, and I mean to scrub the black flag out of her log.
I took her back from the pirates who had made her theirs. I am {name}{rankc}, and she will run honest cargoes under me from now on.
The black flag is struck and she is mine to redeem. I am {name}{rankc}, and I will see her name good again.
We ran the raiders off her and I took command. I am {name}{rankc}, come to bring this hull home to honest trade.
She is clear of the black flag at last, and the keeping of her falls to me. I am {name}{rankc}, and her honest chapter starts here.

founder: I take up the governance of {place}, and this record with it. I am {name}{rankc}.
The rule of {place} is mine now, and its chronicle too. I am {name}{rankc}, and I mean to keep both well.
I set my hand to the governance of {place} this day. I am {name}{rankc}; what befalls this port, I will set down here.
{place} comes into my charge, book and seal alike. I am {name}{rankc}.
The keeping of {place} and its ledger both fall to me. I am {name}{rankc}, and I take them up gladly.
I am {name}{rankc}, and from today the governance of {place} — and the writing of its record — is mine.
overthrow: The mob pulled down the old ruler, and the seal has come to me. I am {name}{rankc}; {place} is mine to govern now.
The streets rose, the old ruler fell, and {place} is mine. I am {name}{rankc}, and I take up its chronicle with its seal.
They cast out the one who ruled before me, and the port is in my hand now. I am {name}{rankc}, keeper of {place} and its book.
{place} threw down its ruler, and the governance came to me. I am {name}{rankc}, and I will write its record from here.
The old order is finished and {place} answers to me. I am {name}{rankc}, come to power on the shoulders of a mob.
The rising put the seal of {place} in my hand. I am {name}{rankc}, and I keep its chronicle now, for better or worse.
graft: The people dragged the old grafter from office and seized the hoard he'd bled from the treasury; the seal — and this record — pass to me. I am {name}{rankc}, and {place} will be kept honestly now.
They found the coffers emptied into one man's coffer and cast him out. I am {name}{rankc}; I take up {place} and its chronicle, resolved to keep clean hands.
The graft is laid bare, the hoarder gone, his coin returned to {place}. It is mine to govern now — I am {name}{rankc}, and I'll not repeat his theft.
piratefall: I took these wharves at the sword's point. I am {name}{rankc}, and {place} is a pirate den now — its black book is mine to keep.
No lawful hand holds {place} any longer — I do, {name}{rankc}, and the black flag flies above it. This log runs red from here.
The magistrate is cast out and the seal broken; {place} answers to me now, {name}{rankc}. Let the record tell of plunder.
redeemed: The black flag is struck and the cutthroats scattered. I am {name}{rankc}, come to restore lawful order over the ruins of {place} and keep its chronicle honestly again.
Privateers broke the den, and {place} returns to the law — under me, {name}{rankc}. I take up its record where the pirates left it bloodied.
The pirate lord is gone, his hoard scattered on the tide. I am {name}{rankc}; {place} is a lawful port once more, and this book is mine.
successor: The rule of {place} passes to me — {name}{rankc}. I keep its chronicle from here.
{place} comes into my keeping after another. I am {name}{rankc}, and its record goes on under me.
The seal of {place} is mine now. I am {name}{rankc}, and I take up its book where the last hand set it down.
Governance of {place} falls to me in turn. I am {name}{rankc}; I keep faith with what came before and set down what comes next.
I take up {place} and its ledger both. I am {name}{rankc}, its ruler and its recorder now.
The care of {place} passes to my hand. I am {name}{rankc}, and I mean to serve it as well as any before me.

{foe} out of {foeHome} put up a poor fight; {we} stripped {goods} bales and {gold}g from her belly and left her the wind to sob into
a fat purse — {we} took {goods} crates of cargo and {gold}g off {foe} and sent her on, lighter and wiser
{we} came alongside {foe} and took what pleased {us}: {goods} bales of goods, {gold}g in coin, and her crew glad to keep their skins
hard pounding, and then {foe} struck to {us} — {goods} bales of cargo and {gold}g the richer, {we} bore away
{we} put a shot through {foe}'s rigging and boarded her at leisure — {goods} bales and {gold}g for {our} trouble
{foe} was slow and {we} were hungry; {goods} bales of cargo and {gold}g changed hands at the cutlass' point
{we} took {foe} without losing a man — {goods} bales of cargo, {gold}g, and a fine day's work

say: {we} hammered {foe} until she filled and went down, her cargo swallowed with her
no prize this day — {we} pounded {foe} beneath the waves and watched the sea close over her
{foe} would not strike, so {we} sent her to the bottom, hold and all
{we} raked {foe} from stem to stern; she slipped under before {we} could take a thing
the guns did their work — {foe} broke apart and sank, and {we} left the deep to have her
{foe} chose the seabed over {our} flag, and {we} obliged her

phrases: , the {ord} port I have put to the torch
— I have shaken off wolves before

say: {foe} came at {us} thinking easy pickings — {we} shot her to splinters and sent her under
a black-flag hull, {foe}, ran down on {us}; {our} gunners were ready and put her beneath the waves
{we} would not be taken — {we} raked {foe} till she burned and slid under, and sailed on unbowed
{foe} misjudged {us}; {our} broadside opened her up and the sea did the rest
they thought {us} a lamb — {we} gave {foe} iron enough to founder her, and kept {our} cargo whole
{we} traded fire with {foe} and won it; she went down and {we} held {our} course

— another wolf I have sent under

say: {we} ran {foe} to ground at last and cut her down — one less wolf on the lanes
the raider {foe} had troubled these waters too long; {we} caught her and sent her under
{we} chased {foe} through the swell and broke her — the sea is the safer for it
{foe} ran, but not far enough; {we} raked her to a wreck and let her sink
{we} hunted {foe} down and gave her no quarter — a pirate's due, paid in full
{we} closed on {foe} and stove her in, and her black flag went down with her

— another bottom out of {foeHome} for the tally
, and not the first {foeHome} crew to rue my flag

pirate: I sail on under the black flag still{bounty}, and take what the sea offers.
She is a rover to this day, and I her master{bounty}.
The black flag flies over her still{bounty}, and I mean to keep it there.
I haunt the trade lanes yet{bounty}, and the honest hulls give me a wide berth.
default: I keep her at sea still, out of {home}.
She runs her cargoes yet, out of {home}, and I keep her book.
We sail on out of {home}, honest and busy, and there is little more to tell.
She is at sea still, {home} her home port, and her log goes on.
I have her yet, out of {home}, and mean to keep her there a long while.

haven: It flies the black flag now — a den of cutthroats, and no lawful hand keeps this book.
The port is a pirate haven now, and no honest ruler writes here.
Cutthroats hold {place} today, and its lawful record ends where the black flag began.
{place} is given over to the black flag — a nest of rovers, and no seal but theirs.
The wharves of {place} answer to pirates now, and there is none left to keep an honest ledger.
default: The port endures under my hand — {population} souls.
{place} holds steady under me, {population} souls in my keeping.
We go on, {population} souls, and the ledger stays calm.
{place} endures — {population} souls, and trade enough to keep them.
The port stands under my hand yet — {population} souls, and steady enough to keep.

ship: Little enough to set down — a quiet life on the trade lanes, and I glad of it.
Not much for the book this while — fair winds, full holds, and no trouble worth the ink.
A calm stretch, and little to record. We trade, we sail, and the sea leaves us be.
Quiet pages these — honest work and easy water, which suits me well enough.
island: Little troubles this port; trade comes and goes, and I keep a calm ledger.
A quiet spell for the port — ships in, ships out, and nothing to alarm the book.
The wharves are calm and the ledger calmer. Little happens worth the setting down.
Trade runs steady and the peace holds; there is not much here to write.
